title: Raman spectra and neural learning distinguish three melanoma cell lines
summary: A neural classifier distinguished Raman spectra from three melanoma cell lines carrying different BRAF or NRAS variants, including a rare BRAF variant. The study collected 50 spectra per line and reported 96.7% accuracy with five-fold spectral cross-validation. This is an in-vitro cell-line measurement, with feature-selection and spectrum-level evaluation caveats; it does not demonstrate independent patient diagnosis or establish that genotype caused the spectral differences.

source_review.scope: Primary relevant Methods/results/limitations and exact front/canonical identity; current primary PubMed linked correction/retraction metadata checked.

evidence.tested: New Raman measurements from three melanoma cell lines, with neural and linear-discriminant spectral classification.
evidence.unknown: Independent cultures, patient-level diagnosis and causal assignment of spectral differences to genotype remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: A feed-forward neural network learns nonlinear boundaries from principal-component Raman features to discriminate the measured cell lines.
